acceptanceCriteria: The target proposal is human-reviewable, links this handoff and both baselines, and contains no unrelated contract change.
avmRequirements: Run the target repository formatting, lint, documentation, examples, test, and AVM pattern-module compliance checks.
compatibilityConstraints: Preserve existing Terraform inputs and outputs; use a reviewed deprecation transition before any removal.
defaultBehavior: Preserve existing Terraform defaults unless a documented migration and semantic-version decision explicitly changes them.
Bicep deploymentMode defaults standalone; Terraform flag_platform_landing_zone defaults true and false selects its network-isolated standalone approximation.
Bicep supports caf and legacy modes with explicit per-resource overrides; Terraform exposes one nullable name_prefix.
Terraform resource_id output is the literal string tbd.

standalone-network-isolated: Require a separate successful approved test deployment plus reviewed DNS, endpoint, reachability, RBAC, and isolation comparison for this scenario.
standalone-standard: Static checks and plan are non-parity evidence; require a successful approved test deployment and reviewed capability comparison for this scenario.

exclusions: Do not implement hub-spoke or arbitrary optional-feature combinations in this proposal unless separately reviewed.
identityRequirements: Prefer managed identity; preserve inventory identity behavior and do not introduce credentials.
appConfig mode grants each workload App Configuration Data Reader; deployment principal receives Data Owner.
Bicep connects Foundry project, Search, and storage identities for configured knowledge sources.
Each Bicep workload receives managed identity, registry pull, runtime configuration, and optional per-app Key Vault access.
principalId and principalType are cataloged separately under identity-rbac.
Workloads and hosted-agent identities receive registry pull; build operators receive scoped task permissions.
migrationPlan: No consumer migration is intended; reject implementation choices that require one and return for review.
networkingRequirements: Preserve scenario-specific public access, private endpoint, DNS, route, subnet, delegation, and dependency-ordering behavior recorded by the inventory.
Bicep environment is external in standard and internal/VNet-integrated with a private endpoint in isolated mode.
Bicep preflight validates mode/network/BYO combinations before deployment.
Bicep uses a private ACR Task agent pool when isolated; existing registries leave private build connectivity to consumers.
Deploy-time App Configuration population occurs only outside isolation; isolated consumers populate through post-provision paths.
deploymentMode=standalone does not itself enable isolation; networkIsolation controls the two assessed topologies.
Knowledge endpoints follow the selected Search/Foundry private connectivity.

owner.source: AI Landing Zone application-platform maintainers; AI Landing Zone maintainers

rbacRequirements: Apply least-privilege RBAC and preserve explicit control-plane and data-plane role boundaries.
appConfig mode grants each workload App Configuration Data Reader; deployment principal receives Data Owner.
Bicep connects Foundry project, Search, and storage identities for configured knowledge sources.
Each Bicep workload receives managed identity, registry pull, runtime configuration, and optional per-app Key Vault access.
principalId and principalType are cataloged separately under identity-rbac.
Workloads and hosted-agent identities receive registry pull; build operators receive scoped task permissions.
requiredBehavior: Bootstrap, location, tags, and deployment metadata: Required deployment identity, locations, tags, deployment topology, release, and stable resource token contracts. Defaults and allowed values are the values on the cited pinned Bicep parameters.
Container Apps environment and workloads: Container Apps Environment, workload profiles, external workload list, per-app ingress/Dapr/identity behavior, and workload outputs.
Container Registry and private ACR Task builds: Registry feature, ACR Task agent pool name/tier/count, private build subnet, and registry endpoint/resource outputs.
Feature flags, software bootstrap, zone redundancy, and preflight: Remaining software, zone-redundancy, and feature output contracts plus deployment-shaping preflight behavior.
Foundry IQ and retrieval-backend configuration: Retrieval backend, Foundry IQ pattern/API/billing/source/storage/search/filter/security configuration, generated keys, connections, and outputs.

CAF and legacy resource naming: CAF/legacy mode, deterministic tokens, explicit resource names, and the names surfaced to consumers. Exact defaults and resource-specific limits remain pinned in main.bicep/main.json.

Runtime configuration modes and App Configuration population: appConfig/containerEnv/none allowed values, App Configuration store, labels, passthrough values, direct bootstrap env vars, and generated runtime keys.

standalone-network-isolated: bootstrap-deployment-contract: partial - Terraform accepts location, resource-group, tags, naming prefix, and a topology flag, but exposes only five sparse outputs; resource_id is the literal string tbd.
resource-naming-contract: partial - Terraform name_prefix cannot preserve Bicep CAF/legacy mode and all explicit resource-name overrides.
container-apps-environment-workloads: partial - Terraform deploys only the Container Apps Environment, not container apps, ingress, Dapr, workload identities, or workload outputs.
runtime-configuration-modes: absent - No App Configuration key-value population or appConfig/containerEnv/none runtime configuration mode exists in Terraform.
foundry-iq-runtime-contract: absent - No Foundry IQ or retrieval-backend configuration, generated keys, or equivalent outputs were found.
container-registry-private-build: partial - Registry exists, but no ACR Task agent pool or equivalent private-build handoff is present.
feature-preflight-zone-software: partial - Terraform validations differ and do not expose Bicep software/bootstrap or general zone-redundancy controls.
standalone-standard: bootstrap-deployment-contract: blocked - Terraform cannot instantiate the public standalone topology. Terraform v0.5.1 structurally requires a VNet, subnets, private endpoints, and mostly disabled public network access, so it cannot represent Bicep standalone-standard.

resource-naming-contract: blocked - Naming alone does not remove Terraform's mandatory private topology. Terraform's naming contract is only usable inside its mandatory VNet/private-endpoint topology, which cannot produce standalone-standard.

container-apps-environment-workloads: blocked - Terraform supplies only an environment and cannot create the Bicep workloads; its global private topology also blocks standard. Terraform v0.5.1 requires the landing-zone VNet/private endpoints and has no Container Apps workload resources, so it cannot represent Bicep standalone-standard workloads.

runtime-configuration-modes: blocked - Terraform creates an App Configuration store but neither Bicep's runtime modes nor populated settings/workloads. Terraform's required private topology prevents the standard scenario, and no App Configuration key-value population/runtime-mode implementation exists.

foundry-iq-runtime-contract: blocked - No Terraform runtime configuration exists and the standard topology is structurally unavailable. Terraform requires private topology and has no Foundry IQ/retrieval-backend runtime configuration contract, so standalone-standard cannot be represented.

container-registry-private-build: blocked - Terraform registry defaults private and cannot form a public standard platform. Terraform registry public_network_access_enabled defaults false with a private endpoint in the mandatory VNet, preventing standalone-standard.

feature-preflight-zone-software: blocked - Terraform has no corresponding standard scenario to validate. Terraform's structural private topology means no preflight selection can produce Bicep standalone-standard.

securityInvariants: Do not store secrets, private environment values, or claim effective isolation from static inspection.
